title: Exclusive: Data Center Cancellations Top $260 Billion in 2026
source_used: Heatmap News (own exclusive); text from WORKDIR/fulltext/C09-03.txt
key_facts: Heatmap Pro data shows at least $260 billion of US data center investment was canceled in 2026 after sustained local opposition.
About $130 billion, roughly half, was canceled in the three months to 30 Sep; third-quarter cancellations in dollars exceeded all of 2025's.
Roughly $1 trillion of data center investment faces sustained or meaningful local opposition; about half of projects that met backlash this year were canceled.
Heatmap calls its figures unpublished, larger than other estimates and likely an undercount, since only about 60% of projects disclose their size.
Most cancellations follow a failed local permit or hostile local government action; hundreds of counties and towns have a ban or moratorium.
An August Heatmap Pro and Embold Research poll found 75% of Americans would oppose a data center near them.
The Data Center Coalition, an industry group, did not respond before publication.
quote_evidence: At least $260 billion of data center investments were canceled this year after sustained local opposition, according to new Heatmap Pro data.
Roughly $1 trillion in data center investment now faces some kind of sustained or meaningful local opposition, according to Heatmap Pro data.
Our investment figures, which have not been previously published and are larger than other estimates, are likely an undercount.
why_it_matters_hint: Local opposition is now cancelling a measurable share of the AI building boom.
notes: Paywall boilerplate sits above the text; article body was read. Single outlet's own survey data, labelled exclusive.
